items.title: 18.8 Stability of Complexes and Stability Constant (Kstab)

source_refs.note: Topic 18.8 with Table 18.5 (printed page 27) and Quick Check 18.6 (printed page 28).

blocks.text: The stability constant (Kstab) is an equilibrium constant (Kc) for the formation of a complex ion. In aqueous solutions, water is the initial ligand. When we add a new ligand, it competes with water to bind with the metal ion. Let us take the example of following equilibrium complexation reaction with its Kstab expression;

Concentration of water [H₂O] being solvent (remains constant) is omitted from the Kstab expression. Stability constants are usually provided on a log₁₀ scale. This makes it easier to compare very large numbers. Higher the log₁₀ Kstab, more stable will be the complex and the equilibrium lies far to the right. And lower the log₁₀ Kstab, the complex is less stable, and the ligands can be easily displaced. The stability constant values (log₁₀ Kstab) of some copper (II) complexes are given Table 18.5.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Table 18.5 prints the ammonia complex as [Cu(NH₃)₆]²⁻. The copper(II) ammonia complex with log₁₀ Kstab = 13.1 is [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ (often written [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺), a positive ion, as in topic 18.7.1.
The data shows that complexes with polydentate ligands have higher stability constant values than those with monodentate ligands. This is called chelating effect of the ligands.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed equation leaves out the charges of the complex ions. With charges it is [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺(aq) + 3en → [Cu(en)₃]²⁺(aq) + 6H₂O(l): en is a neutral ligand, so the complex keeps the 2+ charge of copper(II).

A ligand with a higher Kstab can displace a ligand with a lower Kstab. For example, adding ammonia to a chloride complex will turn the solution blue because the ammonia complex is significantly more stable.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Ammonia replaces the chloride ligands of copper(II) to give the tetraammine complex, not [Cu(NH₃)₆]²⁺: [CuCl₄]²⁻(aq) + 4NH₃(aq) + 2H₂O(l) → [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺(aq) + 4Cl⁻(aq).
Similarly, if a stable complex is diluted with a massive amount of water, the equilibrium can be forced back to the left, re-forming the original hydrated ion.

blocks.title: Quick Check 18.6
blocks.text:
a) Write the Kstab equilibrium expression for the formation of [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺ from [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ and NH₃.
b) Explain why polydentate ligands form more stable complexes using Kstab data (log₁₀ Kstab) data for [CuCl₄]²⁻ (5.6) and [Cu(EDTA)]²⁻ (18.8).
c) Write the balanced equation for the first step of the stepwise substitution of water ligands by ammonia in [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺.
